ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input R(s) enters a summing point with positive and negative signs; the output ω(s) is directly fed back to the negative terminal of the summing point through the lower branch, therefore it is unity negative feedback. The forward path after the summing point is sequentially the gain block K_a, then the DC motor transfer function block 10/(1+10s), with V_a(s) marked between the two blocks, and the final output is ω(s). Reasoning: From the image, the forward transfer function is G(s)=K_a·10/(1+10s). The unity negative feedback closed-loop transfer function is T(s)=G(s)/(1+G(s))=[10K_a/(1+10s)]/[1+10K_a/(1+10s)]=10K_a/(1+10s+10K_a). Write the denominator as (1+10K_a)[1+(10/(1+10K_a))s], so the closed-loop time constant tau_cl=10/(1+10K_a). The time constant of the original open-loop motor transfer function 10/(1+10s) is tau_ol=10. It is required that the closed-loop time constant be 100 times smaller than the open-loop one, that is tau_cl=10/100=0.1. Thus 10/(1+10K_a)=0.1, obtaining 1+10K_a=100, 10K_a=99, K_a=9.9, approximately 10.

method.method_draft: From the text, the motor alone has denominator 1+10s, so its pole is s=-0.1 and tau_ol=10. From the image, the loop transfer is L(s)=K_a*10/(1+10s) with H(s)=1. The closed-loop characteristic equation is 1+L(s)=0, i.e. 1+10K_a/(1+10s)=0, or 1+10s+10K_a=0. Therefore the closed-loop pole is s=-(1+10K_a)/10. A 100-times smaller time constant means the pole should be 100 times farther left than -0.1, i.e. approximately s=-10. Set -(1+10K_a)/10=-10, giving 1+10K_a=100 and K_a=9.9, approximately 10.
